sources.what: DIN 603 table M5-M16 (typos: M6 v min 5.72, M12 P 1.76 -> ignored)
DIN 603 max-value table M6-M20 (P,b,dk,f,k,v); same table as capitalbolts.in, counted once
identical copy of the kova.in table (counted together with it as one source)
small table d2,k,f,b (M20 b-row shifted, not used for M20 b)

dropped.why: M5/M6 have no value for b3 (and jigneshsteel disagrees on M5 b2); M20 b3 listed only by 4; not needed, no nulls allowed
only fuller/fasteners.eu (r) or boltport (e) -> <3 independent sources

checks: dk_max, k_max, f_max, v_max, b, P are strictly non-decreasing M5..M20
max > min for dk, k, f, v in all rows; v_min equals ds_min in all 7 rows (square width min = shank diameter min)
dk_max/d falls from 2.71 (M5) to 2.34 (M20) (all within 2.3..2.8) and k_max < 0.7*d (shallow cup head); dk_max-dk_min = 1.1 (M5,M6), 1.3 (M8-M12), 1.6 (M16,M20)
b(L<=125) = 2d+6 (M5..M16) and 46 for M20 = 2d+6, consistent with ISO coarse-thread bolt rule
v_max > d (square is slightly larger than shank, press-fits into the slot) for all rows; f_max > k_max for all rows
shape_hint: Carriage (coach) bolt: a low shallow-domed round (mushroom) head of diameter dk and height k with no drive; directly under the head a short square neck (height f, width v across flats) that locks into a square hole or wood; below that a plain round shank of diameter d with thread of length b at the end.
notes: Metric DIN 603 (mushroom head square neck bolt, product grade B/C by maker). ISO 8677 (grade C) and KS B 1031 were not separately verified -- they may differ slightly (e.g. tolerances); ASME B18.5 inch carriage bolts are a different table (AFT/Portland/Jignesh list it: 1/4 head dia 0.594, 1/2 1.094) and were NOT collected (only 3 inch sizes have 3 sources). Several pages (Portland/Jignesh inch table 4) show a different 'large head' pattern (1/4: 0.844) -- do not mix with B18.5 carriage bolts. DIN 603 thread lengths b2 (L 125-200: 22,24,28,32,36,44,52) and b3 (L>200: -,-,41,45,49,57,65) are listed by 3-4 sources for M8+, kept out of the table.

verification.checks_done: Re-fetched fuller, fasteners.eu, degademir, boltport, kova, capital live (200); jignesh via raw copy. Parsed all tables; matrix 7 rows x 11 value columns x 7 sources. Only deviations: boltport M12 P 1.76 and M6 v_min 5.72 (copy-typos of the fasteners.eu cluster). Clusters per column (min over rows): P 3 (fuller, feu, degademir; M6-M20 +kova/capital), b 4, dk_max/k_max/f_max/v_max 4-5, dk_min/k_min/f_min/v_min/ds_min exactly 3 (fuller, fasteners.eu, degademir) for ALL seven rows (max-only kova/capital and jignesh give nothing for min columns). Header symbols read from sources: fuller labels f as 'k1' and v as 's'; fasteners.eu and degademir label them f / v ('Neck Height','Neck Width') so the roles are source-defined.
problems: All five *_min columns (dk,k,f,v,ds) rest on exactly 3 clusters (fuller, fasteners.eu, degademir): thin margin - if degademir were judged a copy of the Chinese/FEU data these 35 cells fall to 2

Family label 'ISO 8677 · DIN 603 · KS B 1031 · ASME B18.5' but table is DIN 603 only (ISO 8677 grade C / KS / ASME B18.5 inch carriage-bolt table not verified; ASME B18.5 numbers differ, e.g. 1/2 head dia 1.094) -> publish as DIN 603
ds_min and v_min are identical in every row (redundant column, harmless)
b is for L<=125 only (fasteners.eu prints 'l < 125mm', fuller 'L<=125')
M12 P: 4 clusters 1.75 vs boltport typo 1.76; M6 v_min: 3 clusters 5.52 vs boltport typo 5.72 -> outvoted
